correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts hub-containing and hub-free connected subsets. In the hub case, a rim edge is necessary and sufficient for forcing; in the hub-free case, connected rim subsets force exactly from size three upward. Counting then reduces respectively to complements of cycle independent sets and cyclic intervals. The marked-gap derivation proves the cycle independent-set coefficients. Exhaustive direct simulation for rim orders \(4\) through \(11\) agrees with the classification and every coefficient.

value.rationale: The all-cardinality connected-forcing count is a natural extension of the \(z_c(G;i)\) program in the closest 2025 source, on the standard wheel family that source already singles out for connected-forcing density. The result gives a complete structural classification, an exact polynomial linked to the cycle independence polynomial, the exact minimum-set count \(2n\), and the total count. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the known scalar \(Z_c(W_n)=3\).
